question: Who reconciled Dalton's atomic hypothesis with Gay-Lussac's results on the combination of volumes in 1811?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Amadeo Avogadro**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Amadeo Avogadro** was an Italian scientist who is most famous for his hypothesis known as **Avogadro's Law**.
 
• In 1811, Avogadro proposed that equal volumes of gases, at the same temperature and pressure, contain an equal number of molecules.
 
• This hypothesis was crucial in reconciling **Dalton's atomic hypothesis** with **Gay-Lussac's law of combining volumes**.
 
• Avogadro's ideas were not widely accepted until after his death, but they eventually became a fundamental principle in the field of chemistry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dalton's Atomic Hypothesis**

 
 
• Formulated by John Dalton in the early 19th century, this hypothesis proposed that all matter is composed of indivisible atoms.
 
• Dalton suggested that atoms of a given element are identical in mass and properties, and that chemical reactions involve the rearrangement of these atoms.
 
 
 
• **Gay-Lussac's Law of Combining Volumes**
 
 
• Joseph Louis Gay-Lussac, a French chemist, discovered that gases combine in simple whole-number ratios by volume under the same conditions of temperature and pressure.
 
• This empirical law was key to understanding the behavior of gases and provided a basis for Avogadro's hypothesis.
 
 
 
• **Avogadro's Law**
 
 
• Avogadro's Law states that equal volumes of different gases at the same temperature and pressure contain an equal number of molecules.
 
• This law helped clarify the relationship between the mass and volume of gases, leading to the concept of the mole and Avogadro's number, 6.022 x 10^23 molecules per mole.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Avogadro's Work**
 
 
• Avogadro's contributions laid the groundwork for the development of the ideal gas law, which combines several earlier gas laws into a single equation.
 
• His work also paved the way for the modern understanding of molecular theory and stoichiometry in chemical reactions.
